_about: The districts that held any part of the Santa Clarita Valley in each redistricting plan, with each one's share of the valley's people, for _partials/civic/valley-districts.twig and the body hub on the Assembly, State Senate and House pages (Nathan, 4 October 2026: "every district that held part of the valley, with its share and members, and 'main' as a label rather than a spine"; "Yes, slivers count. The rule is any part of the valley, with the share shown"). Members are read from the office holdings, each term carrying its district number (seatLabel) and plan (districtPlan). From inventory/review/legislative-districts-2026-10-04.md. Acton, outside the valley as counted here, is left out: the 2001-plan 36th Assembly District held Acton and no part of the valley.
method: Shares are of the valley's people. The valley, as counted here, is the Census Bureau's Newhall census county division, the whole City of Santa Clarita as each census drew it, Agua Dulce, and the unincorporated land between the City and Agua Dulce, fixed on the 2020 census map and used for every census (with any unincorporated land the valley wholly encloses); Acton is not included. The people are counted by the archive from census blocks assigned to districts in the official block files of the Statewide Database and the Census Bureau, on the census nearest each plan: 2000 for the 1991 lines, 2010 for the 2001 and 2011 lines, 2020 for the 2021 lines and the 2025 congressional lines. The map draws each district's part of the valley from the same blocks.
sources: California Secretary of State, Statements of Vote, general elections 1992 to 2024, the special election of 4 November 2025 and the primary election of 2 June 2026, https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/prior-elections.

Citizens Redistricting Commission, Final Report on 2011 Redistricting, 15 August 2011, https://statewidedatabase.org/crc_20110815_2final_report.pdf; and Final Maps Report, 26 December 2021, https://wedrawthelines.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/64/2023/01/Final-Maps-Report-with-Appendices-12.26.21-230-PM-1.pdf.

Statewide Database, University of California, Berkeley, district block files for the 1991, 2001 and 2011 plans, https://statewidedatabase.org/; Census Bureau TIGERweb district boundaries for the 2021 plan and the 2025 congressional map.

plans.together: Two members at once: from December 2014 to December 2016 the valley was represented in the Assembly by Scott Wilk for the 38th, holding 93 per cent of its people, and Tom Lackey for the 36th, holding the northeastern 7 per cent. Lackey went on sharing the valley with each member for the 38th, and since 2022 with Pilar Schiavo for the 40th.

california-state-senate.note: A senator serves four years and half the Senate is elected every two, so new lines reach the valley's Senate seat at its next election: the 2001 lines in 2004, the 2021 lines in 2024. Until then the valley kept the senator elected on the old lines.

united-states-house-of-representatives.note: Proposition 50, passed on 4 November 2025 with 64.4 per cent of the vote, replaced the 2021 congressional lines with a map drawn by the Legislature. The primary of 2 June 2026 was held on it, and the members elected on 3 November 2026 take their seats on 3 January 2027. From then the valley is split three ways: the 27th keeps 88 per cent of its people, the 26th takes Castaic, Val Verde and Hasley Canyon, and the 30th takes Agua Dulce and the City's eastern and southeastern edge. In the 27th the June primary's top two were Jason Gibbs and George Whitesides.
